19897-riley-love-lyrics:
James Whitcomb Riley published Riley Love Lyrics in 1883. The Hoosier poet's love poems speak in dialect and plain English alike. One lover finds extra flavor in memory's mellow wine. A little dust of harm, he says, spices the good. He drinks the deeper to that old sweetheart of his. Riley's sentiment is open, musical, and unembarrassed.

Riley was America's most popular poet of his day. His readings filled halls from Indiana to both coasts. Love Lyrics gathers his courtship and remembrance verses. Dialect poems made his fame, but these lyrics show his range. He sings of first loves remembered in middle age. The book is a keepsake from poetry's popular age.

Beech was a manufacturing chemist writing at synthetic dye's high tide. Natural dyes were yielding to aniline colors in the mills. Wool takes dye differently from cotton or silk, fiber by fiber. 20125-a-preface-to-politics:
Walter Lippmann published A Preface to Politics in 1913, his first book, written in his twenties. He attacks a politics stuck on small points of past blame. One case turns on the campaign of 1904 and Theodore Roosevelt. The Senate chased exact guilt in an eight-year-old funds question.

Meanwhile, Lippmann argues, the nation's real needs get no thought at all. He calls for leaders who face new facts with fresh minds. The book made his name as a bold young thinker. Readers still use it to see how modern American political writing began.
20433-women-and-politics:
Women and Politics argues the case about women's place in public life by looking backward first. Its pages survey what earlier ages taught about women. The old charges are set out plainly so the reader can judge them.

Medieval writers, the book notes, blamed women for wild and unbridled passions. They claimed women fell more easily into heresy and witchcraft, and drew attacks from demons, above all if they had beautiful hair. By showing how absurd the old case was, the book clears ground for its claims about women's rights in modern politics.

He aims to join theology to ordinary morals without cant. Handbooks like this one trained ministers and lay readers to reason about right and wrong in a changing, industrial world.

The lectures are technical but lucid, a master's summary of a young science. They preserve the moment when astronomy turned statistical and the galaxy first took measurable shape.
